ordered_prerequisites: A field whose phase-1 join coverage clears 0.60 on a corpus with retained transcripts (the local field's structural ceiling is ~12.6%, so this field cannot qualify without prospective retention changes).
Phase 2 ships a grade report on that field and mints the method_version V.
Phase 3's ledger is deployed and fed with rows for (F, V) — requiring the operator deploy+restart the phase-3 handoff describes.
Phase 4 executes prereg.md as written and returns verdict 'positive' on BOTH eval and holdout (§7.2).
Only then may a phase-5 valve be built, default-off, with arm-B semantics parameterised by the V and the S that run actually produced — and limited to the retrieval-weight channel per §2.6.
what_would_reopen_phase_5.the_idea_is_not_refuted: Nothing here tests whether transcript-grounded silent-recall reinforcement helps. It was never measured. The blocker is transcript disk retention on the local field, upstream of the hypothesis.

why_the_valve_could_not_be_built_even_if.consequence: An ON valve would read an absent table for a field/method_version pair that does not exist and apply a strictness rule nobody selected. It would be a no-op wearing the evidence of an experiment that was never run.
why_the_valve_could_not_be_built_even_if.summary: This is the finding that goes beyond the gate. The contract requires a valve whose ON semantics match the replay A/B's arm B 'exactly as pre-registered'. Those semantics are parameterised by two values that only a completed phase 2 and a completed phase-4 run can supply. Both are undefined. A valve claiming to match arm B would therefore have had to invent its own semantics and mislabel them as pre-registered — the precise failure the contract warns against ('a valve that applies different semantics than the A/B measured invalidates the operator's evidence for enabling it').
